subject.title: Feishu: duplicate final replies can occur after model failover from rate-limited primary

question: Should this be fixed as a Feishu-local recovery guard, a shared same-turn final identity contract, or folded into the broader durable final-delivery contract?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves later finals after Feishu error closeout, while the merged shared dedupe only handles byte-identical final entries; choosing where to collapse or replace failed-attempt output is a product and owner-boundary decision.

options.title: Narrow Feishu Recovery Guard
options.body: Make Feishu keep or replace the errored-attempt card during transient failover and deliver only the recovered fallback final for that user turn, with explicit tests for distinct diagnostics.

options.title: Shared Final Identity Contract
options.body: Define a cross-channel same-turn final identity rule so failed-attempt and recovered-fallback duplicates collapse in the shared dispatcher without losing intentional repeated finals.

options.title: Fold Into Durable Delivery Roadmap
options.body: Track this only under the broader durable final-delivery contract and defer a Feishu-local fix until that cross-channel design is ready.

recommendation.title: Narrow Feishu Recovery Guard
recommendation.body: Make Feishu keep or replace the errored-attempt card during transient failover and deliver only the recovered fallback final for that user turn, with explicit tests for distinct diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent Feishu error-final history and are a good owner for deciding whether the current later-final-after-error behavior should be narrowed.
